If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings from negative to positive over 3–5 days, shift forecast upward by 2–4% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.00–0.33) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for lack of directional signal.

If sentiment peaks at +1.00 and holds for 2+ days, add 3–5% upward bias in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect strong bullish sentiment persistence.

If sentiment shows repeated negative spikes (≥2) in last 5 days, apply 2–4% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to hedge against volatility or reversal risk.
